name: Kamil Crater, Egypt
matches: Rayed ejecta, normally seen only on airless or thin-atmosphere bodies; iron meteorite impactor
breaks: Sandstone target, not lunar regolith; one small crater; Earth air
mission_tasks: Impact geology, ejecta mapping, sample collection practice
key_facts: 45 m wide; under 5,000 years old; found on Google Earth imagery in 2008; 5,178 iron meteorite pieces (about 1.71 tons) recovered
geology: Cretaceous sandstone target; ungrouped iron meteorite

name: Kharga yardangs (Western Desert), Egypt
matches: Yardangs, crescent dune trains and wind streaks like those seen from Mars orbit; core of the largest hyperarid region on Earth
breaks: Hot, not cold; Earth air pressure
mission_tasks: Rover driving over yardangs; sand abrasion tests
key_facts: USGS and Smithsonian field studies in 1978 to 1984 compared its landforms with Mars; little since. About 200 km west of the Nile
geology: Yardangs carved in limestone, Nubian sandstone and old lake sediments

name: Lut Desert (Dasht-e Lut), Iran
matches: Hottest land surface measured from orbit; huge daily temperature swing; large yardang fields
breaks: Hot extreme, while Mars and the lunar poles are cold; thick air
mission_tasks: Thermal stress tests of hardware; rover driving on yardangs
key_facts: MODIS recorded 80.8 °C surface (2002 to 2019 study); daily swing up to about 71 °C; dunes up to 470 m tall
geology: Salt desert; dark sand blackened by volcanic lava

name: Western Qaidam Basin, China
matches: Highest desert on Earth: cold, dry, high UV; salt playas; yardangs and polygons similar to those on Mars
breaks: Still has air, liquid water and life
analog_for: Mars (Gale crater and Medusae Fossae yardangs; salt playas)
mission_tasks: Rover tests; instrument tests on salts and clays; biosignature search
key_facts: Yardang fields cover tens of thousands of sq km (counts range 20,000 to 38,800); evaporation 2,590 mm/yr. Coordinates are a published yardang sample site
climate_notes:
Elevation (m): >2,700
Mean annual temp (°C): 3.5 (air; July avg 16, Jan avg -10.7)
Precip (mm/yr): <20
geology: Lake sediments, salts, chlorite and illite clays, carbonate nodules

name: Bodélé Depression, Chad
matches: Largest single dust source on Earth; wind lifts dust from a dry lake bed
breaks: Dust is diatomite from an old lake; Earth air is far denser
mission_tasks: Dust mitigation; dust storm forecasting; wind and abrasion tests
key_facts: Produces roughly half the dust leaving the Sahara; dust lifts on about 65% of days; part of Lake Megachad about 7,000 years ago

name: Harrat Khaybar and Umm Jirsan lava tube, Saudi Arabia
matches: Large basalt volcanic field with a long lava tube that preserved artifacts for thousands of years
breaks: Lunar tubes may be up to about 1 km wide, far larger; Earth gravity
analog_for: Moon and Mars (lava tube shelters); Moon (basalt)
mission_tasks: Habitat-in-cave tests; underground navigation; radar detection of tubes
key_facts: Umm Jirsan: 1,481 m long, about 45 m wide, ceilings up to about 12 m. Field 12,000 to 14,000 sq km; last eruption about 650 CE. Coordinates are the volcanic field's

name: Lonar Crater, India
matches: One of very few craters formed in basalt; target rock similar to Martian basaltic meteorites; ejecta like Martian fluidized ejecta
breaks: Has a lake and vegetation; monsoon climate; Earth air
analog_for: Mars and Moon (small craters in basalt)
mission_tasks: Impact geology in basalt; sampling; ejecta studies
key_facts: 1.88 km wide; about 37,500 years old by one dating method (others differ); hydrothermal clays formed after impact
geology: Deccan Traps basalt; saponite, celadonite, carbonate

name: Dallol, Danakil Depression, Ethiopia
matches: Polyextreme hot, hypersaline, hyperacidic brines (pH down to -1.7); some pools have no life despite liquid water
breaks: Far hotter and wetter than Mars; active volcanism
analog_for: Mars (salts, acid brines, limits of life)
key_facts: Dallol dome is 48 m below sea level; the surrounding Danakil Depression floor is about 120 m below. Mean annual air temp about 35 °C. Hot-spring fluids reach 108 °C (water, not ground)
climate_notes:
Elevation (m): -48 (Dallol dome)
Mean annual temp (°C): 35 (air, mean)
Precip (mm/yr): <50 typical (up to 144)
geology: Evaporites (halite and other salts), iron minerals

name: Río Tinto (Peña de Hierro), Spain
matches: Acidic (mean pH 2.3), iron-rich river depositing jarosite and iron oxides like those Opportunity found at Meridiani
breaks: Wet Mediterranean climate; vegetation; Earth air
key_facts: River 92 km long; source at Peña de Hierro, 689 m; NASA's MARTE project simulated a robotic Mars drilling mission here in 2005. Coordinates: Peña del Hierro visitor-center parking (approximate)
geology: Jarosite, schwertmannite, goethite, hematite; massive pyrite

name: East Antarctic Plateau cold spots
matches: Coldest surface on Earth, about -98 °C snow surface
breaks: Lunar shadowed craters stay near -233 °C (40 K), far colder; ice sheet, not regolith
mission_tasks: Cold-soak tests; shows how far Earth falls short
key_facts: About -98 °C seems to be close to the coldest Earth's surface can get; coldest spots in shallow dips near the Dome Argus to Dome Fuji ridge. Coordinates: Dome Argus summit, a reference point near the coldest spots
climate_notes:
Elevation (m): about 3,500
Extreme temp (°C): -98 (snow surface, satellite)

name: Atacama Desert (Yungay), Chile
matches: Driest non-polar desert; highest UV on Earth; perchlorates as on Mars
key_facts: Mean precipitation mostly below 4 mm/yr in the hyperarid core, 0.15 mm in some spots; studied as a Mars analog since 2003. Coordinates: Yungay (abandoned town), approximate

name: Haughton Crater, Devon Island, Canada
matches: Only known impact crater in a polar desert; permafrost; cold, dry, dusty, high summer UV
breaks: Liquid water in summer; Earth air and gravity
geology: Impact breccia with permafrost; shale, siltstone, gneiss

name: Malapert Massif
matches: Kamil and Lonar (craters); Harrat Khaybar (basalt, tubes); East Antarctic Plateau (cold, partly)
key_facts: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole (Oct 2024 list)
climate_notes:
Gravity (m/s²): 1.62
Surface pressure: 0 (vacuum)
Surface temperature: Diviner (LRO) ground surface: maximum about 320 K (47 °C) toward the ridge's upper elevations, about 220 K (-53 °C) near its base. Summit averages about 180 K in summer and 130 K in winter. Long-lit polar spots in general: about -50 ± 10 °C
Ice and water: Near permanently shadowed regions that may hold water ice
geology: Mountain massif with about 1,250 m of relief; candidate landing area slope 5.6° ± 2.0°; a candidate landing spot is a relatively flat area above a 5,000 m cliff

name: Arcadia Planitia
key_facts: Ice-rich northern plain; SWIM's pilot study region; proposed landing site for robotic and crewed missions
climate_notes:
Gravity (m/s²): 3.73
Surface pressure: 6.36 mb average (4.0 to 8.7 by season), under 1% of Earth's
Surface temperature: Not measured here. Proxy only: at the Viking 1 lander site, AIR temperature 1.6 m above the ground ranged -89 to -31 °C over a day (NASA fact sheet). Not a ground temperature
Ice and water: Shallow ground ice; excess ice widespread in the mid-latitudes
geology: Flat plain of lava flows up to 3 billion years old; yardangs; dust devils seen by Mars Express
